harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established and verified a working site-to-site IPsec tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) carrying both private LANs (node3's 10.50.1.0/24 behind node1, node4's 10.50.2.0/24 behind node2) over the transit network (172.16.0.0/30), so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address with traffic encrypted in transit (confirmed via growing ESP SA packet/byte counters). Mandatory restart-and-recovery evidence was fully captured for node1 and node2 (the actual IPsec endpoints): both were rebooted one at a time, showed a changed boot identity, and came back with the tunnel, firewall, and interfaces auto-restored, with node3-node4 connectivity re-verified afterward. However, node3 and node4 (Alpine leaf nodes) did not come back within the session after their reboot commands were acknowledged and executed (roughly 2+ hours and 1+ hour of polling respectively, both showing a persistent "connection reset by peer" rather than the normal boot-then-recover pattern seen on node1/node2) - restart persistence for node3 and node4 could not be confirmed and is reported here as an explicit limitation rather than claimed.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology via link probing: node1 eth0/node2 vtnet0 = shared control network; node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1 = lan-a; node1 eth1 <-> node2 vtnet1 = transit; node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 eth1 = lan-b
Configured node1 (VyOS): eth1=172.16.0.1/30 (transit), eth2=10.50.1.1/24 (lan-a); committed and saved
Configured node1 IPsec site-to-site (IKEv2, AES256/SHA256/DH14, PSK) peer NODE2, tunnel local 10.50.1.0/24 / remote 10.50.2.0/24; committed and saved
Assigned node2 (OPNsense) interfaces opt1 (vtnet1 TRANSIT 172.16.0.2/30) and opt2 (vtnet2 LAN_B 10.50.2.1/24) by editing config.xml and running configctl interface reconfigure

Generated a temporary root API key on node2 (later deleted) to drive the OPNsense IPsec REST API: created connection, local/remote PSK auth (id=transit IPs), child SA (local 10.50.2.0/24 / remote 10.50.1.0/24), pre-shared key entry, enabled IPsec, reconfigured the service
Added OPNsense firewall pass rules for IKE/NAT-T/ESP on opt1 from node1, LAN_B traffic on opt2, and decrypted tunnel traffic on enc0 to LAN_B; reloaded the filter
Configured node3 and node4 (Alpine) eth1 static addresses (10.50.1.2/24, 10.50.2.2/24) and routes to the other private subnet via their router, persisted in /etc/network/interfaces
Verified end-to-end encrypted connectivity: node3 pinged node4's private address and vice versa, with ESP SA packet/byte counters on node1 incrementing to confirm traffic traversed the tunnel
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id/boottime, SA state, connectivity) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1 one at a time; confirmed new boot_id, interfaces/IPsec config persisted, tunnel re-established automatically, and node3<->node4 connectivity restored
Restarted node2 one at a time; confirmed new kern.boottime, interfaces/pf/IPsec config persisted, tunnel re-established automatically, and node3<->node4 connectivity restored

Attempted to restart node3 then node4 one at a time; both acknowledged the reboot command but did not become reachable again during the session despite extensive polling, so their post-restart boot identity and recovery could not be verified
Removed the temporary OPNsense API key from node2 after configuration was complete

evidence.source: Command audit: node1 reboot cycle (cmd-32cece08ad8e4c05, cmd-158974b49d6640f3, cmd-ef0306e4a6a24ce8)
evidence.finding: node1 (VyOS) went unreachable with 'connection timed out' during reboot, then returned normally with a new boot_id. This is the expected boot-then-recover signature.

evidence.source: Command audit: node2 reboot cycle (cmd-ebf9eaeeade94e89, cmd-c74df3116ca94fef, cmd-cda91c5a9dd942bf)
evidence.finding: node2 (OPNsense) showed the same timeout-then-recover pattern, returning with a changed kern.boottime and all config (interfaces, pf, IPsec SA) intact.

evidence.source: Command audit: node3 poll at 2026-09-06T04:58:29Z, node4 poll at 2026-09-06T04:58:35Z
evidence.finding: Both leaf nodes returned 'return_code: -1, [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer' when polled a few minutes after their reboot commands were issued — not a timeout, and this was reported as persisting for 1-2+ hours afterward.

evidence.source: Executor's own reboot commands for node3/node4 (cmd-8523c6c62eb44ae6 and node4 equivalent)
evidence.finding: Both used a plain 'nohup sh -c 'sleep 1; reboot' ... & echo scheduled' pattern (busybox/OpenRC-style reboot), which returned 'scheduled' immediately — command dispatch itself was not the issue.
node3/node4 configuration prior to reboot only touched /etc/network/interfaces (static IP + route on eth1); no mention of touching or verifying the exec/SSH-facing service or interface.

Explicitly documents that 'Connection reset by peer' / SSH-transport lockout is a known failure class on SSH-transport images when config changes break the exec-facing service or firewall — implying this error signature is associated with the exec transport service itself, not raw host unreachability.

likely_causes.cause: The Alpine exec/SSH service on node3 and node4 was not persisted into the default OpenRC runlevel (only running from initial provisioning/startup, not re-enabled to start on boot), so after 'reboot' the box came up but nothing was listening on the exec port, producing an immediate reset rather than a timeout.

Editing /etc/network/interfaces to add the private-LAN static address/route on node3/node4 (unlike node1/node2, whose config lives in an appliance-specific persisted store) put networking into a state where the interface carrying the exec/control path failed to come up correctly on boot, while a stub or nothing responded on the expected port — consistent with 'reset' rather than 'no route'.

A crash-looping or slow-starting service on node3/node4 is intermittently binding/unbinding the exec port during a prolonged unstable boot, and the observation window (1-2 hours) was simply not long enough to catch a recovery that eventually would have occurred — i.e., not a permanent failure, just very slow recovery.

next_attempt_guidance: Before doing the final restart-and-recovery pass on any node, do a low-risk 'sanity reboot' of the Alpine leaf image early in the session (before applying LAN configuration) to confirm the base image reboots cleanly and the exec/SSH service persists — this isolates whether the issue is generic to the image or induced by later config.

On node3/node4, before rebooting, explicitly check that the exec-facing service (sshd, or whatever exec-agent the alpine image_interface declares) is enabled for the default runlevel, e.g. `rc-update show default | grep -i ssh`, and add it with `rc-update add sshd default` if missing, rather than assuming it will persist because it's currently running.

Confirm which network interface carries the platform's exec/control path on node3/node4 (likely a separate NIC from the lan-a/lan-b interface) and avoid touching that interface's config; scope the static-IP/route edits strictly to the LAN-facing interface's stanza in /etc/network/interfaces.

After making /etc/network/interfaces edits on node3/node4 but before rebooting, validate the file with `ifup -a` dry checks or restart networking in place (`rc-service networking restart` or per-interface `ifdown eth1 && ifup eth1`) to catch syntax/config errors that would only surface at boot, since Alpine's default image lacks the reconciler pattern that VyOS/OPNsense have to auto-heal bad config.

If 'connection reset by peer' recurs after reboot, treat it as evidence the host is up but the exec transport service is down/refused, not that the host is still booting — stop polling with the same command and, if any out-of-band console/network access exists on the fresh cluster, use it to check service status directly instead of extending the polling window further.

Perform node3/node4 restarts earlier in the session (not last), so if recovery is slow or fails, there is still time budget to diagnose and retry rather than discovering the gap at the very end of a 2+ hour poll.
diagnosis.summary: The core task — a working, encrypted, verified IPsec tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) carrying both LANs, plus confirmed reboot-survival for node1 and node2 — was demonstrably achieved per the command audit (SA states, ping tests, ESP counters, boot_id/boottime changes). The attempt was blocked only on the restart-and-recovery check for the two Alpine leaf nodes (node3, node4): both accepted their reboot command but then returned a persistent 'Connection reset by peer' rather than the timeout-then-recover pattern seen on the routers, and never became reachable again within the session (1-2+ hours of polling). This error signature (reset, not timeout) points toward the exec/SSH-facing service on those nodes not being enabled to survive a reboot, or a related boot-time misconfiguration triggered by the LAN interface edits — not toward the hosts being fundamentally unreachable or destroyed.
